description: The LIVE MONEY PATH pair, design.md 5 row 4b-i: F-5 (conditional-failure detection reads error.response['Error']['Code'] through order_keys.is_conditional_failure, never str(error), across six sites) and F-2 (the webhook review arm yields to the native one through a GUARDED resolve_payment_reference that can never replay a captured payment). Grouped because both edit amplify/functions/payments/razorpay-webhook/handler.py and both target the same two functions (wecare-razorpay-webhook, wecare-invoice-engine), which design.md confirms were NOT touched by the parallel session - so this pair carries no O11 dependency and is the more urgent half of 4b-i. Depends on FEAT-001 only for the anchor merge and the ordering constraint, not for content. Two commits, one per F-item. Corresponds to plan.md Part A items 3 and 4. The DEPLOY is OWNER CONFIRM (O10) per function, plan.md Part B row B2 - do not deploy.
steps: STEP 0 - read .kiro/work/deep-integration-audit/task-deep-integration-audit/context.json and this file FIRST, then plan.md Part A items 3 and 4. Re-derive every anchor on the merged tree; if FEAT-001's findings record a line-number difference, that record wins over plan.md's number.

F-5 STEP 1 - re-derive the six sites: `git grep -n "ConditionalCheckFailedException' in str" -- amplify/functions/payments` (expect FIVE, all in razorpay-webhook/handler.py at :1719, :2036, :2149, :2746, :2866) and `git grep -n "ConditionalCheckFailedException' not in str" -- amplify/functions/payments` (expect ONE, invoice-engine/handler.py:853). order_keys.is_conditional_failure already exists at amplify/functions/shared/lambda_utils/ecommerce/order_keys.py:177 and is UNCHANGED by this FEAT.

F-5 STEP 2 - convert PER SITE, NOT MECHANICALLY. The five razorpay-webhook sites become `if order_keys.is_conditional_failure(<err>):` preserving each site's own variable name (guard_err at :1719, e at :2036, cond_err at :2149, e at :2746, e at :2866). invoice-engine/handler.py:853 is NEGATED and becomes `if not order_keys.is_conditional_failure(claim_err):`. DO NOT INVERT :853 - inverting it turns an expected duplicate-invoice race into a 500 and a real storage failure into a silent dedup hit, on the GST-sequence path at :843-852, which is the most consequential of the six.

F-5 STEP 3 - no import change is needed. order_keys is already module-scope at razorpay-webhook/handler.py:37 (with the comment at :36 recording it is import-safe: creates no client, reads no secret at import) and at invoice-engine/handler.py:48. Leave the five redundant function-local re-imports in the webhook (:479, :814, :974, :1020, :2553) alone.

F-5 STEP 4 - EIGHT further substring sites are deliberately OUT OF SCOPE and must not be touched: core/contacts/handler.py:527 :589 :617; messaging/inbound-whatsapp-handler/handler.py:3280 :7858; messaging/outbound-whatsapp/handler.py:4078; messaging/whatsapp-business-api/flows/postpay.py:169; shared/lambda_utils/flow_completion.py:242. They are not on the captured-payment path and sweeping them in would widen a LOW-severity change across five more functions.

F-5 STEP 5 - write tests/test_conditional_failure_detection.py, two halves failing TODAY IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. Half 1 needs a TEST-LOCAL subclass, because a plain ClientError cannot carry the code with the substring absent (botocore interpolates Error.Code into MSG_TEMPLATE, so str(err) always contains it): `class OpaqueConditionalFailure(ClientError): def __str__(self) -> str: return 'storage error'`, instantiated with ({'Error': {'Code': 'ConditionalCheckFailedException', 'Message': 'storage error'}}, 'UpdateItem'). Assert the premise first - "ConditionalCheckFailedException" not in str(OPAQUE) - and that order_keys.is_conditional_failure(OPAQUE) is True. Then assert the five webhook sites take the IDEMPOTENT branch (info log, no duplicate side effect) and invoice-engine:853 takes the DEDUP-HIT branch (info invoice_dedup_hit_atomic, no 500). Half 2 needs no subclass: a plain ClientError with Code='ValidationException' and Message containing '... ConditionalCheckFailedException ...'; assert EVERY site takes the ERROR branch. NO production subclass of ClientError is introduced - the subclass lives in the test module only, and is_conditional_failure itself is unchanged.

F-5 STEP 6 - run the new file (see it fail, then pass), then `-k "razorpay or invoice or webhook"`, then the whole suite. Commit F-5 with its test, staging exact paths only: amplify/functions/payments/razorpay-webhook/handler.py, amplify/functions/payments/invoice-engine/handler.py, tests/test_conditional_failure_detection.py.

F-2 STEP 1 - re-derive the insertion point: `git grep -n '_request_review_on_whatsapp(invoice_id, contact' -- amplify/functions/payments/razorpay-webhook/handler.py` (the call site, :2469) and `git grep -n 'BOTH legs ask' -- <same>` (the FAIL-OPEN comment block, :2458). The block to replace is :2468-2470.

F-2 STEP 2 - replace it with EXACTLY the form specified in plan.md Part A item 4, including the four-line comment, which is part of the specification because it is the only record of why the guard exists: set `native = False`; inside a try, `payref = order_keys.resolve_payment_reference(dynamodb.Table(COMMERCE_KEYS_TABLE), reference_id) or {}` and `native = bool(payref.get('nativeCatalogService'))`; `except order_keys.OrderIdentityUnavailable:` log a WARNING json with event 'review_native_check_unavailable', referenceId and requestId; then `if contact and invoice_id:` - when native, log an INFO json with event 'review_request_skipped_native', referenceId and requestId; else call _request_review_on_whatsapp with the existing five arguments unchanged.

F-2 STEP 3 - no new plumbing and no new import. COMMERCE_KEYS_TABLE is module-level at :101, dynamodb.Table(COMMERCE_KEYS_TABLE) is already the idiom at :2555 and :2621 in this same file, json is imported at :22, logger = get_logger(__name__) at :39, and reference_id and request_id are already in scope and already passed to _request_review_on_whatsapp.

F-2 STEP 4 - THREE THINGS ARE BINDING AND MUST NOT BE 'TIDIED'. (i) The default on an unreadable PAYREF# row is native = False, i.e. WE SEND THE REVIEW. A duplicate review nudge during a storage outage is strictly preferable to replaying a captured payment. NEVER invert this to 'skip on error' - that would make a transient throttle silently suppress a legitimate website review request, which is the silent-partial-success class this audit exists to find. (ii) Catch order_keys.OrderIdentityUnavailable SPECIFICALLY, not bare Exception: order_keys._read_row:344-347 wraps every storage error into that one type, so the narrow catch has NO storage blind spot, while a bare catch would also swallow a genuine programming error (bad table name, missing attribute, non-mapping result) and turn it into a permanently invisible duplicate-review bug. That asymmetry is the whole point: a storage outage must fail open on a captured payment, a logic bug must be loud. (iii) review_request_skipped_native is at INFO so the suppression is greppable rather than silent, matching post_payment_flow_skipped at :1703, :1720, :1731.

F-2 STEP 5 - do NOT change order_keys._read_row or its raise-on-storage-error contract (order_keys.py:335-347); its docstring at :336-341 records why a read failure must never be reported as absence. Do NOT change the native senders (flows/paid_submit_request.py, flows/paid_vault.py) - the webhook arm is the one that yields, because the native trigger asks after the service was actually delivered while the webhook asks at capture.

F-2 STEP 6 - write tests/test_native_service_review_dedup.py, five cases, driving the real razorpay-webhook post-payment function and the real paid_submit_request.review(...) against one shared fake commerce-keys/ServiceRequests pair, with both outbound boundaries spied (lambda_client.invoke and urllib.request.urlopen). (1) test_one_native_purchase_asks_for_a_review_once - nativeCatalogService True and detailsSubmittedAt set; EXACTLY ONE invoke carries templateName == 'wecare_leave_review' (two are sent today). (2) test_a_website_purchase_still_asks_once - nativeCatalogService absent; the website leg still sends exactly one. Sensitivity proof that the fix did not simply disable the webhook arm. (3) test_a_paid_native_purchase_with_no_details_asks_for_no_review - nativeCatalogService True, NO detailsSubmittedAt; ZERO review invokes. Pins the design's decision that no fulfilment implies no review invitation. (4) test_an_unreadable_payment_reference_does_not_fail_the_capture - the fake commerce-keys table raises botocore.exceptions.ClientError with {'Error': {'Code': 'ProvisionedThroughputExceededException'}} on get_item; assert IN THIS ORDER OF IMPORTANCE that the post-payment function returns normally and does not raise, that the handler does NOT return 500, that EXACTLY ONE review invoke happened (the fail-open default), and that review_native_check_unavailable was logged at WARNING.

F-2 STEP 7 - test case (5) is the one that is easy to get wrong: test_an_error_outside_the_storage_wrapper_is_not_swallowed. INJECT OUTSIDE _read_row's try, or the test proves nothing and reports red on the most dangerous change in the plan. A KeyError raised by table.get_item arrives at the guard AS OrderIdentityUnavailable (because _read_row:344-347 wraps every storage exception) and is correctly caught. So instead monkeypatch the module's `dynamodb` resource so .Table() raises KeyError('COMMERCE_KEYS_TABLE') - it is evaluated BEFORE resolve_payment_reference is entered, so it cannot be converted. (Alternative: stub resolve_payment_reference to return a non-mapping truthy value such as [1], so `or {}` passes it through and .get() raises AttributeError.) Assert the exception PROPAGATES out of the post-payment function rather than being absorbed into the fail-open default, and that NO review invite was sent on that call. This pins the narrow-catch choice so a later tidy-up to `except Exception` fails the suite.

F-2 STEP 8 - run the new file (see the first and fourth cases fail, then pass), then `-k "razorpay or webhook or payment"`, then the whole suite. Commit F-2 with its test, staging exact paths only: amplify/functions/payments/razorpay-webhook/handler.py, tests/test_native_service_review_dedup.py.

FINAL STEP - set this FEAT's status to completed and record in findings: the whole-suite count after each of the two commits, the two commit SHAs, and anything a later FEAT needs (in particular, confirm that razorpay-webhook/handler.py now has both the F-5 conversions and the F-2 guard so FEAT-003/004 do not re-edit it).

=== 1. THE TWO COMMIT SHAs AND THE WHOLE-SUITE COUNT AFTER EACH ===
F-5 commit aca7fdd4ec506090bd9d33dc64ff6f1f1e4f40e0 - 'fix: decide a conditional failure on the money path from the error code, never the message'. 3 files, +384/-6. Whole suite AFTER this commit: 1 failed, 10460 passed, 6 skipped, 3 xfailed in 112.57s.

Whole suite AFTER this commit: 1 failed, 10469 passed, 6 skipped, 3 xfailed in 111.51s (re-run of the same command confirmed 10469 twice).
The gate FEAT-001 set was `passed >= 10432 with the ONE inherited failure and no other`. Both runs meet it: 10460 then 10469, strictly rising, and the only failure in either is the inherited tests/test_github_oidc_trust_policy.py::test_fixer_covers_every_oidc_role_the_repository_declares (the GitHubActions-wecare-digital-payment-deploy-temp-20261009 OIDC role that arrived with upstream 4ee4c498 and is unregistered at origin/stack too). It is an IAM-TRUST matter, out of scope, deliberately NOT fixed. THE GATE FOR FEAT-003 ONWARD IS THEREFORE: passed >= 10469 with that one failure and no other.

=== 4. THE TWO SAFETY POINTS, EACH CHECKED EXPLICITLY ===
(a) THE NEGATION IS PRESERVED, NOT INVERTED. invoice-engine/handler.py:889 reads `if not order_keys.is_conditional_failure(claim_err):`. Verified by grep after the edit and pinned by two tests that would both fail if it were inverted: test_an_opaque_conditional_failure_is_a_dedup_hit_in_the_invoice_engine (statusCode 200, deduplicated True, info invoice_dedup_hit_atomic, no invoice_claim_error) and test_a_substring_lookalike_is_a_500_in_the_invoice_engine (statusCode 500, invoice_claim_error, no dedup hit). The GST-sequence path at :869-888 is untouched.
(b) THE F-2 GUARD IS EXACTLY AS SPECIFIED. Default on an unreadable row is native = False, i.e. WE SEND THE REVIEW - pinned by test_an_unreadable_payment_reference_does_not_fail_the_capture, which asserts EXACTLY ONE review invoke on a throttled PAYREF# read; inverting the default to 'skip on error' makes that assertion fail. The catch is `except order_keys.OrderIdentityUnavailable:` and NOT bare Exception - pinned twice, behaviourally by test_an_error_outside_the_storage_wrapper_is_not_swallowed and source-level by test_the_guard_catches_the_storage_type_and_not_everything, which slices the Step-5 block out of the handler source and asserts 'except Exception' does not appear in it. A later tidy-up to `except Exception` fails both.

=== 5. THE REPLAY RISK WAS PROVEN ABSENT, NOT ASSUMED ===
The danger F-2 carries is that a transient DynamoDB error becomes a 500 that lets the idempotency lease lapse and lets Razorpay replay a captured payment. tests/test_native_service_review_dedup.py proves the absence through the REAL top-level handler rather than by inspection: _route_captured signs a real HMAC over a real payment.captured body, patches _get_webhook_secret to a test-only value so the REAL _verify_signature runs, and uses the real _complete_event path. test_a_throttled_native_check_still_answers_the_provider_200 asserts statusCode 200, the lease COMPLETED exactly once, and one review sent, with the commerce-keys fake armed to raise botocore ClientError ProvisionedThroughputExceededException on get_item. Its sensitivity partner test_the_rig_would_have_caught_a_500_and_an_abandoned_lease raises OrderIdentityUnavailable in the same rig and asserts statusCode 500 AND completed == [] - so the 200 above means 'the guard works' rather than 'the rig cannot see a failure'. NOTE for anyone reading the design: the design says case 4 'fails today because revision 2's unguarded form propagates'. On THIS tree there was no resolve call at all before the fix, so the pre-fix failure is the missing review_native_check_unavailable WARNING, not a propagated exception. The replay property is covered by the two handler-level cases above instead.

The 16 failures are the two halves failing in OPPOSITE directions, confirmed by reading the assertion output per site (e.g. handle_refund logged refund_update_error/ERROR under the opaque failure, and logged refund_status_not_applied/INFO under the substring lookalike). After the conversions: 19 passed.
F-2: tests/test_native_service_review_dedup.py was verified failing-first by saving the guard as a patch, `git checkout HEAD -- <the one file>`, running (5 failed / 3 passed), then `git apply` to restore and re-confirming 8 passed. No stash, no reset, no history rewrite. The three that pass both before and after are deliberate: test_a_website_purchase_still_asks_once (the sensitivity proof that the fix did not simply disable the webhook arm), test_the_rig_would_have_caught_a_500_and_an_abandoned_lease, and test_a_throttled_native_check_still_answers_the_provider_200.
